source: RC1 deep review, the coordinator's third batch, 2026-11-23; RFC 0004 §4.5.3, RFC 0009 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: A token revocation is kept past the end of every token it can name, so no revoked token is valid again when its record expires: the starter keeps a token's or a subject's revocation for the longer of cosec.jwt.token-validity.access and cosec.jwt.token-validity.refresh, plus cosec.authentication.revocation.skew (an issuer's clock may run that far ahead, IDN-29), computed and never configured, and the control plane's check that a revocation outlives an approval reads the same value. No token outlives that retention: CoSec's issuer refuses a call that asks for an access or refresh validity longer than the configured one, naming the property.
